description: An upright shrub 1-2.5 m tall of several erect stems with rough, grey-green, sweet-and-sharp smelling lobed leaves, and hanging clusters of pink flowers that open in the middle of winter, from November to March, when little else is in bloom. It grows on dry chaparral slopes and the sunny edges of oak woodland, feeds the first hummingbirds of the year, and its dusky purple berries in late spring are eaten by jays, quail, foxes, coyotes and bears.

season_notes.winter: Fresh grey-green leaves came back with the rains, and drooping clusters of pink flowers hang along the stems from November to March, the hummingbirds' winter food.
season_notes.spring: Full leaf; the last flowers fade in March and berries ripen dusky purple with a pale bloom in April to June.
season_notes.summer: Leaves dry, yellow and drop in the summer drought; by July the shrub is mostly bare grey-brown stems.
season_notes.fall: Bare stems until the first rains, then new leaves and the first pink buds in November.

notes: Chaparral currant is a deciduous shrub 1-2.5 m of dry chaparral slopes, the sunny edges of oak woodland and foothill pine woodland, from the Coast Ranges to the Sierra foothills. Form: plain 'shrub'. Four to seven erect stems from the base, spreading little (stem_spread 26), with short ascending side shoots (level-1 down angle 36, tropism up): an upright shrub a little taller than wide, the opposite of the gooseberry's low spread; envelope W/H about 0.9. Unarmed (no spines, unlike the gooseberry). Bark red-brown to grey, shredding on old stems (shreddy). Leaves alternate, 2-6 cm, round, three- to five-lobed, rough and hairy above, felted below, grey-green, with a sharp, resinous smell: leaf_shape lobed, leaf_size_m 0.045; the palette lightens a fifth of the leaves for the pale felted undersides. Summer-deciduous: the leaves dry and drop in the summer drought (mostly bare July to October; leaf_on_by_month reaches 0.02 in August and September, where the generator switches the cards to the bare-twig texture, so the stems read bare) and come back with the first fall rains, so the leaf-on curve is the reverse of a winter-deciduous shrub's (high December to May) and the winter colour is the fresh new leaf, not the twigs. Flowers in drooping racemes of 10-25, pink to rose, from November to March, often on bare or just-leafing stems (before_leaves true): flowers months [11, 3], which the generator's month test wraps across the new year (decoActive), so the November start is drawn. Berries round, about 1 cm, dark purple under a whitish bloom (rgb a dusky purple), glandular-hairy, April to June. Hummingbirds (Anna's hummingbird above all) depend on it in winter; they are not among the game's animals, so they are named in the description only. Architectural model provisional.
